_about: The statements of the text, computed from the paper's own tables (arithmetic) and from our run (observed);

text_contaminated_negative.statement: When the data were contaminated, the relative biases were all negative (Results).

fields.name: Table 1: every relative bias of the contaminated rows is negative (96 values)

text_outcome_rate.statement: Scenarios with lower outcome rates seemed to be associated with more elevated absolute relative biases (Results).

fields.name: Table 1: |bias| at outcome 10% exceeds |bias| at 25%, every contaminated cell and model (32 pairs)
Table 1: |bias| at outcome 25% exceeds |bias| at 40%, every contaminated cell and model (32 pairs)

text_linear_gap.statement: With a linear Z the largest differences occurred at 5% contamination and 10% outcome, where the log-binomial models had 3.5%-6.7% higher biases (Results).

fields.name: Linear Z: the largest LB - RP gaps in |bias| are at 5% contamination and 10% outcome
Linear Z, 5% contamination, 10% outcome: smallest gap (points)
Linear Z, 5% contamination, 10% outcome: largest gap (points)

text_nonlinear.statement: With a non-linear Z the robust Poisson model outperformed the log-binomial model when the data were contaminated, visibly even at 2%; a larger difference went with smaller outcomes (Results).

fields.name: Non-linear Z: RP less biased than LB in every contaminated cell (24)
Non-linear Z: RP less biased than LB in every 2% cell (12)
Non-linear Z: the gap is larger at outcome 10% than at 40% (8 pairs)

text_se_uncontaminated.statement: Without contamination the SEs of the two models were identical at the 2nd decimal point (Results).

fields.name: Table 2, 0% rows: LB and RP SEs equal at the 2nd decimal in all 24 pairs
Table 2, 0% rows: LB and RP SEs differ by less than 0.005 before rounding (24 pairs)

text_se_contaminated.statement: With contamination the SEs remained comparable at outcome rates of 25% and 40%; at 10% the log-binomial SEs seemed slightly higher in some scenarios (Results).

fields.name: Table 2, contaminated rows at outcome 10%: LB SE above RP SE in some cells
Table 2, contaminated rows at outcome 25% and 40%: LB and RP SEs within 0.01 in every cell

text_mse.statement: The MSEs follow the pattern of the biases: comparable with a linear Z except at outcome 10% and 5% contamination; with a non-linear Z the models diverge even at 2% (Results).

fields.name: Table 3, linear Z: LB MSE exceeds RP MSE by more than 0.005 only at outcome 10% and 5% contamination
Table 3, non-linear Z: LB MSE at least RP MSE in every 2% cell (12), as printed

text_n500.statement: With n = 500 the same pattern was observed and the SEs were larger (Results, Additional file 2).

fields.name: Table A2 SE above Table 2 SE in every cell (144)
Table A1, non-linear Z: RP less biased than LB in every contaminated cell (24)

text_no_outliers.statement: Without outliers the study did not observe any difference in biases or variances between the two models, for n = 1500 and n = 500 (Discussion).

fields.name: 0% rows of Tables 1 and A1: LB and RP relative biases within 0.5 points in all 48 pairs

text_main_claim.statement: Comparable models with a linear confounder; the robust Poisson model consistently outperforms the log-binomial model with a quadratic confounder, even at 2% contamination (Abstract, Discussion, Conclusions).

fields.name: Linear Z: LB and RP |bias| within 2 points in every contaminated cell except outcome 10% at 5%
Non-linear Z: RP less biased than LB in every contaminated cell, from 2% on (24)

text_convergence.statement: COPY (C = 1,000,000) converged in all 1,000 simulations in all 48 scenarios with the linear confounder and in 30 of 48 with the non-linear one; in the other 18, convergence rates 0.983-0.999 (median 0.996) (Discussion).

fields.name: Linear Z: scenarios with every log-binomial fit converged (of 48)
Non-linear Z: scenarios with every log-binomial fit converged (of 48)
